'''Richard Rowland Skemp''', {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|sep=,|FBPsS}} (10 March 1919 – 22 June 1995) was a British mathematician, psychologist and academic, who specialised in [[mathematical education]]. Having started his career as a school teacher, he became a lecturer in psychology at the [[University of Manchester]] in 1955. He was appointed Professor of [[Educational Theory]] at [[Warwick University]] in 1973 and also served as director of its Mathematics Education Research Centre from 1978 until he retired in 1986.

==Biography==
Skemp was born on 10 March 1919 in [[Bristol]], England.<ref name="obit Ind">{{cite news |last1=Brown |first1=Margaret |author1-link=Margaret Brown (mathematics educator) |title=Obituaries: Professor Richard Skemp |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/obituaries-professor-richard-skemp-1589629.html |access-date=11 January 2025 |work=The Independent |date=2 July 1995}}</ref> His father, Professor Arthur Rowland Skemp, had been killed in action during the First World War on 1 November 1918.<ref name="obit Times">{{cite news |title=Professor Richard Skemp - Obituary |work=The Times |date=25 July 1995}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Arthur Rowland Skemp |url=https://www.ww1.manchester.ac.uk/roll-of-honour/arthur-rowland-skemp/ |website=WW1 Centenary |publisher=University of Manchester |access-date=11 January 2025}}</ref> As a foundation scholar, he was educated at [[Wellington College, Berkshire|Wellington College]], then an all-boys [[independent school (UK)|independent school]] in Berkshire which had been set up for the sons of deceased army officers.<ref name="Warwick tribute">{{cite web |last1=Tall |first1=David |author1-link=David Tall |last2=Thomas |first2=Michael |title=RICHARD SKEMP March 10, 1919 – June 22, 1995 |url=https://homepages.warwick.ac.uk/staff/David.Tall/pdfs/dot2002b-skemp-tribute.pdf |website=Warwick University |access-date=11 January 2025 |pages=i-iii |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240413033345/https://homepages.warwick.ac.uk/staff/David.Tall/pdfs/dot2002b-skemp-tribute.pdf |archive-date=13 April 2024}}</ref> He won an open scholarship in mathematics at [[Hertford College, Oxford]], matriculating in 1937.<ref name="Warwick tribute" /> 

His university studies were interrupted by military service during the [[Second World War]].<ref name="obit Times" /> On 24 May 1941, having trained at an [[Officer Cadet Training Unit]], he was commissioned in the [[British Army]] as a [[second lieutenant]] to serve in the [[Royal Corps of Signals]].<ref name="LG 6 June 1941">{{London Gazette |issue= 35186 |date= 6 June 1941 |pages= 3314–3316 |supp= y |city= |title= |quote=}}</ref> He served in India and had reached the rank of captain by the end of the war.<ref name="Warwick tribute" />

After the end of the war, Skemp returned to Oxford to continue his studies.<ref name="Warwick tribute" /> He graduated from the [[University of Oxford]] with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] (BA) degree in 1947.<ref name="obit Times" /> He then worked as a mathematics teacher at two [[Private schools in the United Kingdom|private schools]]; first [[Oundle School]] and then at [[Rye St Antony School]].<ref name="obit Times" /> After developing an interesting in how children learn, he returned to Oxford to undertake a second undergraduate degree in psychology in 1952.<ref name="Warwick tribute" /> He then moved to the Department of Education, [[University of Manchester]] to undertake a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (PhD) degree under the [[Doctoral supervisor|supervision]] of [[C. E. M. Hansel]] and Professor John Cohen.<ref name="obit Ind" /><ref name="thesis">{{cite thesis |last= Skemp |first= Richard R. |date= 1958 |title= Investigation into difficulties in learning mathematics by children of good general intelligence |degree= PhD |publisher= University of Manchester |url= https://www.librarysearch.manchester.ac.uk/permalink/44MAN_INST/bofker/alma993030234401631 |accessdate= 23 February 2025}}</ref> He completed his PhD in 1959 with a [[doctoral thesis]] titled "Investigation into difficulties in learning mathematics by children of good general intelligence".<ref name="obit Ind" /><ref name="thesis" />

Skemp joined the academic staff of the University of Manchester as a [[lecturer]] in psychology in 1955. He was promoted to [[senior lecturer]] in 1962. In 1973, he joined the [[University of Warwick]] as Professor of Educational Theory. He also served as director of the Mathematics Education Research Centre at Warwick from 1978 to 1986.<ref name="obit Ind" /> He retired from full-time academia in 1986, but continued to lecture around the world.<ref name="Warwick tribute" /> He was [[visiting professor]] at the [[University of Calgary]] from 1987 to 1994.<ref name="obit Ind" />

==Personal life==
In 1961, Skemp married Valerie Watts.<ref name="obit Ind" /> Together they had one son.<ref name="obit Ind" /> In January 1995, Skemp was diagnosed with [[non-Hodgkin's lymphoma]].<ref name="Warwick tribute" /> He died on 22 June 1995, aged 76, in [[Coventry]], England.<ref name="obit Ind" />

==Selected works==

* {{cite journal |last1=Skemp |first1=Richard R. |title=Reflective Intelligence and Mathematics |journal=British Journal of Educational Psychology |date=February 1961 |volume=31 |issue=P1 |pages=45–55 |doi=10.1111/j.2044-8279.1961.tb01701.x}} 
* {{cite book |last1=Skemp |first1=Richard R. |title=The psychology of learning mathematics |date=1971 |publisher=Penguin Books |location=Harmondsworth |isbn=9780140212105 |url=https://archive.org/details/psychologyoflear0000skem_a4c9}}
* {{cite journal |last1=Skemp |first1=R. R. |title=Relational understanding and instrumental understanding |journal=Mathematics Teaching |date=1976 |volume=77 |issue=1 |pages=20–26 |url=https://atm.org.uk/write/mediauploads/resources/richard_skemp.pdf}}
* {{cite book |last1=Skemp |first1=Richard R. |title=Intelligence, learning, and action: a foundation for theory and practice in education |date=1979 |publisher=Wiley |location=Chichester |url=https://archive.org/details/intelligencelear0000skem }}
* {{cite book |last1=Skemp |first1=Richard R. |title=Mathematics in the primary school |date=1989 |publisher=Routledge |location=London |isbn=978-0415025195}}
